evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires positive, unequal manager PIDs and nonempty, unequal invocation IDs. It never requires the manager snapshot pair to share a nonempty boot ID. A guest reboot between the two manager snapshots can change both PID and invocation ID, so the check passes even though the observations span a reboot; the separate `boot_id_changed` check only covers the planned reboot pair. Adding the nonempty/equal boot-ID condition while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks is a small correctness fix, not a new requirement needing owner judgment.
